description: Locked ticker-to-sector-ETF mapping for the 24-ticker Phase 2 universe, GICS-sector-consistent. See SPEC section 7.1. This is a BENCHMARK-DESIGN CHOICE for computing a relative-return control -- it is not an assertion that any of these ETFs are the 'correct' peer group in an alpha-generating sense, and 'stock minus sector_etf' is never called an abnormal return or alpha anywhere in this codebase (see derivations.relative_return docstring). A later remap requires a new mapping_version, never an in-place edit.
reviewed_by: claude-sonnet-5 (sourced desk review via live web search/fetch against current ETF-holdings and GICS-classification sources -- not a domain-expert manual sign-off; treat as a documented, source-backed automated review)
review_notes: All 24 assignments individually checked against each candidate sector ETF's actual current holdings list (companiesmarketcap.com fund-holdings pages, retrieved 2026-08-04) and/or GICS sector classification (web search, retrieved 2026-08-04). 23 of 24 are confirmed current constituents of their assigned sector ETF. GPN was corrected from XLK to XLF (see its own review.reason below) -- confirmed ABSENT from XLK's 77 holdings and PRESENT in XLF's holdings at 0.24% weight, consistent with the real GICS reclassification of the 'Transaction & Payment Processing Services' sub-industry from Information Technology to Financials (2023 GICS structure update). GME is the one remaining documented ambiguity: its GICS sector is confirmed Consumer Discretionary (source-backed), the same defensible rule used for every other ticker, but it could NOT be confirmed as a current constituent of XLY's disclosed ~50-holding list at review time -- left visibly unresolved (see GME's own review block) rather than silently asserted as fund-verified. This does not block APPROVED status: every entry has either a fund-membership confirmation or a documented, sourced, defensible GICS-sector rule, and the one open question is stated plainly, not hidden.
